newsitem.title: USA: Marvel vp confirms talks in bankruptcy case. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Marvel vp confirms talks in bankruptcy case. [CORRECTED 22:25 GMT]

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Group Inc vice president of finance August Liguori confirmed on Thursday earlier statements by an attorney for the company indicating that all parties in the contentious Chapter 11 bankruptcy case were holding talks.
"There are some discussions going on among the parties," Liguori told Reuters after a hearing Thursday before U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Helen Balick.

In a rare display of harmony, attornies for Marvel Holdings Inc bondholders and for the lead bank of Marvel Entertainment's secured lender, Chase Manhattan Bank, sought and received from Balick a postponement from June 16 to July 17 of the hearing date for any disclosure statements.

The court must approve the adequacy of a disclosure statement -- the financial condition of a debtor -- before it can consider whether to confirm a reorganization plan that would allow a company to emerge from Chapter 11 protection.

Balick also allowed Marvel Entertainment to suspend interest payments to Chase on its $100 million debtor-in- possession financing. Marvel attorney Harvey Miller told Balick that "because of continuing cash losses of Marvel Entertainment's operations," it expects to use up the remaining $8 million of its DIP money before the end of June.
According to court papers "The debtors have intitiated negotiations with Chase...regarding additional post-petition financing" to avoid having to suspend operations.

Competing reorganization plans have been proposed by bondholders, led by Carl Icahn, and the debtors, including Marvel and its secured lenders. Each plan contemplated at different times joining forces with Toy Biz Inc, in which Marvel also has a stake.
(Corrects to show that only one plan has been submitted to the Bankruptcy Court. Also corrects identity of debtors).

On May 29, Toy Biz said it and the bondholders had elected to terminate their joint proposal to bring the comic book publisher out of bankruptcy. A spokesman for the bondholders said Perelman pressured Toy Biz to withdraw. Later that day, Marvel denied that it was behind Toy Biz's decision to withdraw from the joint reorganization.

When Miller told Balick that mediation suggested last week by U.S. District Court Judge Roderick McKelvie was opposed by bondholders, she warned all attorneys she would "put a cap on fees" unless they tried to "close down this litigation."

After the hearing Thursday Toy Biz attorneys David Fleischer and David Stratton told Reuters there were "discussions going on all the time about a wide range of issues." They declined to comment more specifically.
Toy Biz has urged that a mediator be appointed, but the court has no authority to do so unless requested by the parties.

"We've all seen mediation be extremely effective when the parties can bridge the gap themselves," Fleischer said. "Toy Biz talks to everyone," he said in response to a question about whether Toy Biz was included in any talks. But Fleischer added "I don't think there's been any movement...Nothing today affected Toy Biz."
